content: Southampton Hospital, located in Southampton, New York, is a 168-bed facility and the only hospital serving the Hamptons region. Notably, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, the former First Lady of the United States, and her sister Lee Radziwill were born at this hospital. It is a member of the NewYork-Presbyterian Healthcare System. The hospital admits over 6,000 patients annually and handles approximately 26,000 emergency room visits each year, with half of these visits occurring during the summer season. The hospital's origins trace back to 1908 when Dr. Wheelwright and Dr. Schenck performed an emergency surgery by kerosene light in the attic of a Southampton house because there was no time to transfer the patient to the nearest hospital. The patient survived, and this event led to the establishment of the hospital. Initially, the doctors rented two rooms in a house on Hampton Road to serve as a hospital. As demand grew, cots were placed in hallways, and additional rooms were rented. In 1909, the Southampton Hospital Association purchased the Hervey J. Topping house at the corner of Lewis Street and Meeting House Lane, planning to build a hospital on an adjacent lot. The current hospital, located on a five-acre property on Old Town Road stretching from Meeting House Lane to Herrick Road, opened in 1913. Since then, the hospital has undergone significant expansion. Southampton Hospital benefits from funds raised at the Hampton Classic Horse Show, one of the most prominent social events of the summer season. The hospital is affiliated with several healthcare facilities and centers, including the Westhampton Primary Care Center, Centers for Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in East Hampton and Westhampton Beach, the David E.D. Center for HIV/AIDS Care, the Shinnecock Indian Health Clinic, the Southampton Care Center (a skilled nursing facility), the Southampton Hospital Regional Dialysis Center, the Center for Prenatal Care in Greenport, and diagnostic centers in East Hampton and Hampton Bays. In 2006, the Berger Commission, aiming to streamline medical costs in New York State, recommended downsizing Southampton Hospital to 125 beds and merging it with Eastern Long Island Hospital in Greenport and Peconic Medical Center in Riverhead. The commission also strongly suggested that Brookhaven Memorial Medical Center in Brookhaven join the merged entity. Despite the proposed merger, the hospitals would continue to operate as separate facilities. The commission further recommended formal affiliation with Stony Brook University Hospital. In 2007, Southampton Hospital announced plans to consider selling its 12-acre property, located in a residential neighborhood, and constructing a new hospital closer to a highway. While no specific location was disclosed, reports noted that 400 of the hospital's 600 employees reside west of the Shinnecock Canal.
